DISCRIMINATORY JOB ADVERTISEMENTS AND APPLICANT INQUIRIES (FEHA) — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Acme, Inc.

ABOUT THIS DISCRIMINATORY JOB ADVERTISEMENTS AND APPLICANT INQUIRIES INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes a restriction that California's Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) places on job advertisements, publications, and pre-employment inquiries, and how that restriction — codified at Government Code section 12940(d) — relates to Acme, Inc.'s consideration of Jordan T. Reyes for Marketing Coordinator. Government Code section 12940(d) makes it, subject to listed exceptions, an unlawful employment practice for an employer or employment agency to print or circulate, or cause to be printed or circulated, any publication, or to make any nonjob-related inquiry of an employee or applicant — whether verbal or made through an application form — that expresses, directly or indirectly, a limitation, specification, or discrimination based on a list of characteristics the statute names, or any intent to make such a limitation, specification, or discrimination.

This corpus separately includes a California Fair Pay Act — Information Sheet, a CROWN Act: Race-Based Hairstyle Discrimination in Hiring — Information Sheet, a Genetic Information Nondiscrimination Act (GINA) — Information Sheet, a Religious Accommodation in Employment (FEHA) — Information Sheet, a Post-Offer, Pre-Employment Medical Examination — Information Sheet, and a Driver's License Requirement in Job Postings — Information Sheet, each addressing a different, more specific statutory provision; this document addresses section 12940(d)'s general restriction on discriminatory publications and applicant inquiries, not those other provisions. This document states facts about what section 12940(d) says and whom it covers; it does not evaluate Acme, Inc.'s specific job advertisement, application form, or interview questions, and it does not determine whether any particular publication or inquiry complies with the statute. This document is not itself a job advertisement, an application form, or a determination of compliance with the statute described, and it does not tell Acme, Inc. or Jordan T. Reyes what to do about any particular hiring material or inquiry.

THE BONA FIDE OCCUPATIONAL QUALIFICATION AND SECURITY REGULATION EXCEPTIONS
Government Code section 12940's introductory clause states that the unlawful employment practices listed in the subdivisions that follow — including subdivision (d)'s restriction on discriminatory publications and applicant inquiries — do not apply where the practice is based upon a bona fide occupational qualification, or, in specified circumstances, where it is based upon applicable security regulations established by the United States or the State of California.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "It is an unlawful employment practice, unless based upon a bona fide occupational qualification, or, except where based upon applicable security regulations established by the United States or the State of California:"
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12940 (California Legislative Information text), California Government Code § 12940, introductory clause (bona fide occupational qualification and security regulation exceptions) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12940.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes only the statute's introductory clause; the statute's text at this location does not itself define "bona fide occupational qualification" or specify which security regulations qualify, leaving those terms to sources outside this section's text. This document does not determine whether a bona fide occupational qualification or security regulation exception applies to Acme, Inc.'s specific job advertisement, application form, or inquiry.

THE RESTRICTION ON DISCRIMINATORY PUBLICATIONS AND APPLICANT INQUIRIES
Government Code section 12940(d) states that it is an unlawful employment practice (subject to the exceptions described above) for an employer or employment agency to print or circulate, or cause to be printed or circulated, any publication, or to make any nonjob-related inquiry of an employee or applicant — whether verbal or made through use of an application form — that expresses, directly or indirectly, any limitation, specification, or discrimination as to race, religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, age, sexual orientation, reproductive health decisionmaking, or veteran or military status. The prohibition also reaches any intent to make such a limitation, specification, or discrimination, not only an inquiry or publication that actually results in one.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "For any employer or employment agency to print or circulate or cause to be printed or circulated any publication, or to make any nonjob-related inquiry of an employee or applicant, either verbal or through use of an application form, that expresses, directly or indirectly, any limitation, specification, or
						discrimination as to race, religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, age, sexual orientation, reproductive health decisionmaking, or veteran or military status, or any intent to make any such limitation, specification, or discrimination."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12940(d) (California Legislative Information text), California Government Code § 12940(d), discriminatory publication and applicant-inquiry prohibition (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12940.)
  Known gap: This clause's quoted text includes an embedded line-wrap (a newline followed by a run of tab characters) between "specification, or" and "discrimination as to race" that appears in the leginfo.legislature.ca.gov HTML source itself as formatting whitespace produced by the page's line-wrapping, not as a substantive break in the statutory sentence; it is reproduced here exactly as it appears in the source rather than corrected, consistent with how this corpus treats other confirmed HTML line-wrap artifacts. This clause does not address subdivision (e)'s separate, narrower restriction on medical or psychological examinations and inquiries, which this corpus's Post-Offer, Pre-Employment Medical Examination — Information Sheet already addresses; nor does it resolve what falls within the term "nonjob-related," which the statute's text does not itself define at this location.

EXCEPTION FOR AGE INQUIRIES COMPELLED OR PROVIDED FOR BY LAW
Government Code section 12940(d) states that its restriction on discriminatory publications and inquiries does not prohibit an employer or employment agency from inquiring into the age of an applicant, or from specifying age limitations, where the law compels or provides for that action.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "This part does not prohibit an employer or employment agency from inquiring into the age of an applicant, or from specifying age limitations, if the law compels or provides for that action."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12940(d) (California Legislative Information text), California Government Code § 12940(d), age-inquiry exception (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12940.)
  Known gap: This clause does not resolve which other statutes "compel" or "provide for" a given age inquiry or age limitation; the statute's text at this location does not enumerate them. This document does not determine whether any such law applies to a specific age-related inquiry or limitation by Acme, Inc.

WHICH EMPLOYERS SECTION 12940(D) COVERS
FEHA's definitions section, Government Code section 12926(d), states which entities are an "employer" for purposes of FEHA's unlawful-practices provisions, including the discriminatory-publication and applicant-inquiry restriction described above. It states that "employer" includes any person regularly employing five or more persons, or any person acting as an agent of an employer, directly or indirectly, the state or any political or civil subdivision of the state, and cities, and it separately excludes a religious association or corporation not organized for private profit from that definition.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "“Employer” includes any person regularly employing five or more persons, or any person acting as an agent of an employer, directly or indirectly, the state or any political or civil subdivision of the state, and cities"
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12926(d) (California Legislative Information text), California Government Code § 12926(d), general employer definition (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12926.)
  "“Employer” does not include a religious association or corporation not organized for private profit."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12926(d) (California Legislative Information text), California Government Code § 12926(d), religious-association exclusion (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12926.)
  Known gap: The statute's text does not itself state how the "five or more persons" threshold is counted — for example, over what time period, in what location, or whether part-time or out-of-state personnel are included — leaving that computation to sources outside this section's text. This same definitions section, Government Code section 12926(d), is also cited by other documents in this corpus that address other subdivisions of section 12940; it is being independently re-verified here (fetched separately, twice, with distinct User-Agent strings, for this document) for use in this document.

WHICH EMPLOYMENT AGENCIES SECTION 12940(D) COVERS
Government Code section 12940(d)'s restriction applies to an "employment agency" as well as to an "employer." FEHA's definitions section, Government Code section 12926(e), defines "employment agency" to include any person undertaking, for compensation, to procure employees or opportunities to work.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "“Employment agency” includes any person undertaking for compensation to procure employees or opportunities to work."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12926(e) (California Legislative Information text), California Government Code § 12926(e), employment agency definition (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12926.)
  Known gap: The statute's text at this location does not state a minimum number of placements, a minimum fee amount, or any other threshold that distinguishes a covered "employment agency" from other compensated activity, and it does not resolve whether any specific person or business meets this definition. This corpus separately includes a California Fee-Charging Employment Agency Regulation — Information Sheet addressing a different statutory scheme (the Employment Agency, Employment Counseling, and Job Listing Services Act, Civ. Code §§ 1812.500 et seq.), which defines "employment agency" differently and for a different regulatory purpose than this FEHA definition; this clause does not restate that separate definition.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT
This information sheet regarding Government Code section 12940(d)'s restriction on discriminatory job advertisements and applicant inquiries was reviewed by Acme, Inc. in connection with Jordan T. Reyes's prospective position of Marketing Coordinator on September 9, 2026. It reflects the statutory text as of the date checked in each authority section above and does not reflect any amendments made after that date, and it is not a substitute for consulting a licensed attorney.

Reviewed by (on behalf of Acme, Inc.): ______________________
Date: September 9, 2026
